title: Names That Nearly Were
question: Was Xbox always called Xbox?
placard: My son and I were watching a documentary about the Xbox when we learned the name was only ever meant to be temporary. It turns out a lot of famous names were nearly something else entirely — some ridiculous, some forgotten, some saved by a misheard word or a trademark search that ran out of time.
summary: Famous names that began as placeholders, near-misses and happy accidents: Xbox, Bluetooth, Sherlock Holmes, James Bond, Amazon and more.

title: From Quill to Keyboard
question: Did you use to write on a typewriter, Dad?
placard: Yes, I did — and correction fluid too, the cheaper kind. To my son, the past is one flat place where I might as well have been chiselling stone tablets. This gallery gives it some depth: how we got from reeds and feathers to the keys under your fingers.
summary: How writing and printing evolved, from papyrus and goose quills to movable type, the typewriter and correction fluid.
